title: Merging Strategies & Conflict Resolution
description: Combine lines of development with fast-forward and three-way merges, decipher conflict markers, and resolve collisions cleanly.

blocks.content: When you've finished work on a branch, you merge it back into another branch (usually `main`). Merging combines the histories of two branches into one.

## Merging a Branch

First switch to the branch you want to merge *into*:
```
git switch main
```

Then merge the other branch:
```
git merge feature/login
```

If there are no conflicting changes, Git completes the merge automatically.

## Merge Conflicts

A conflict happens when both branches changed the same part of the same file in different ways. Git can't choose which version is correct, so it stops and asks you to decide.

Git marks the conflict in the file like this:
```
<<<<<<< HEAD
This is the version from your current branch
=======
This is the version from the branch being merged in
>>>>>>> feature/login
```

To resolve it:
1. Open the file and edit it to what it should actually say
2. Remove the `<<<<<<<`, `=======`, and `>>>>>>>` lines
3. Stage the resolved file: `git add filename`
4. Complete the merge: `git commit`

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["git merge feature/login"] --> B{"Any conflicts?"}
    B -- No --> C["Merge commit created automatically"]
    B -- Yes --> D["Git marks conflicts in files"]
    D --> E["Edit files to resolve"]
    E --> F["git add resolved files"]
    F --> G["git commit to finish"]
```

Merging brings work from one branch into another. Usually Git can combine different changes, like fitting two edits into different paragraphs.

A conflict means Git found two competing edits to the same spot and needs a human decision. It is a question, not proof that someone failed.

blocks.question: What does a merge conflict mean?
options: The branch is too large to merge
Both branches changed the same part of the same file and Git needs you to decide which version to keep
You don't have permission to merge
The branches have been apart for too long
blocks.explanation: A conflict means Git found two competing edits to the same part of the same file and cannot automatically decide which is correct. You open the file, choose what the content should be, stage it, and commit to complete the merge.

blocks.prompt: Merge the branch feature/login into the currently checked-out branch.
